Without ensurepip, `python3 -m venv` cannot bootstrap pip at all - this is a missing stdlib module, not a sandbox permission quirk. `python3 -c "import axelrod"` also raises ModuleNotFoundError. This is why the 2026-10-02 doer run could not complete task 1, and why three consecutive reviews ranked an unexecutable task first.

Environment (NEW, risk) - the ambient interpreter is Python 3.14 while this repo's own deleted pyenv markers named 3.11.11, i.e. the original coursework ran on 3.11. Axelrod may have no 3.14 wheels, so even a working pip may not resolve `pip install axelrod` on this interpreter.

GameTheoryIMATMT/Bayes_Player.py:34 - off-by-one in the TitForTat likelihood. Re-derived this review and confirmed: at the turn where self.history and opponent.history each hold t entries, opponent_move is the opponent's round t-1 move, which a TitForTat copies from the agent's round t-2 move = self.history[-2]. The code compares against self.history[-1], which only tests whether both players happened to play the same action in the same round - near-50/50 noise, so the TitForTat hypothesis never receives real evidence.

GameTheoryIMATMT/Bayes_Player.py:30 - cooperation_ratio is computed over self.history (the agent's own actions) and then used at :40 as evidence about the opponent's type; the MajorityBased belief update is self-confirming.

GameTheoryIMATMT/Bayes_Player.py:46 - recent_defections counts the agent's own defections as evidence for ThresholdBased, and the guard `len(self.history) > 5` around a `[-5:]` slice forces the value to 0 for the first six turns.

GameTheoryIMATMT/Bayes_Player.py:13-22 - strategy_categories maps categories to opponent class names, but the lists are never read anywhere in the file; only the dict keys and len() are used. Many names are invented and absent from Axelrod (GrimTrigger, Forgiver, Stochastic_TitForTat, ForgivingTitForTat, FriendlyGrudger, RiskyCooperator); Grudger is the real one.

GameTheoryIMATMT/Bayes_Player.py:53-58 - likelihoods are pinned at 0.1/0.9 with no floor, so priors decay geometrically and lock near zero permanently; combined with Turns = 10 at :91 (nine updates) the posterior cannot converge, so the experiment's horizon is too short to test its own hypothesis.

GameTheoryIMATMT/Bayes_Player.py:99-104 - results record only scores, never max(self.priors, key=...), so a run cannot answer whether the opponent's type was identified - the only question main_question.md actually asks.
GameTheoryIMATMT/Bayes_Player.py:7-25 - BayesianAI subclasses axl.Player but defines no `classifier` dict, unlike every stock Axelrod strategy.

GameTheoryIMATMT/HPC/ai_player.py:48 - response[-PLAYS:] takes the last 50 characters of the decoded output, which still includes the echoed prompt because the input ids are never stripped; :53 maps anything that is not literally "C" to Defect, making the LLM player a defect-heavy random player.

GameTheoryIMATMT/HPC/ai_player.py:18,22 - the prompt is handed opponent.__class__.__name__, i.e. the opponent's exact identity, which removes the very information asymmetry main_question.md is about; it is also never given the match history.
GameTheoryIMATMT/HPC/tournament.py:21-25 - result dicts set "Strategy" to opponent.name and "Opponent" to scores[0] (a score stored under a name key); strategy.name and scores[1] are never recorded.

GameTheoryIMATMT/HPC/plots.py:15 - results[row[0]] = int(row[1]) keys a dict by name across a ~240x240 loop, silently keeping only the last match per name, and row[1] holds a score mislabelled as Opponent by tournament.py.

GameTheoryIMATMT/Strat_per_strat.py:70-77 - while True exits only on ai_response == "✅" while the prompt at :43 asks for "Y✅", and the response is the full decoded prompt+completion; the condition can never fire. :74 would raise TypeError anyway (strategies is a list indexed there by strategy name), and :20 passes device_map="none", not a valid value. It fails first at :29 reading results/Strategy_Guide_results.json, which .gitignore excludes and which is absent.
GameTheoryIMATMT/Initial_match.py:81 - module-level reference to `i`, which is local to the loop inside plot_results; NameError after all ~57,600 matches have run.

GameTheoryIMATMT/Initial_match.py:25-26 - total_scores accumulates both players for every ordered pair, so each unordered pairing is counted twice and self-matches add both scores to the same key; the ranking is roughly 2x inflated. The whole loop reimplements axl.Tournament single-threaded.

GameTheoryIMATMT/*.sh - all four SLURM scripts confirmed by grep to be copy-pasted from an ANSYS Fluent CFD template: each carries `module load fluent` (:25) and `--licenses=anshpc:176` (:15) on a PyTorch job, plus `#SBATCH -D /users/adgz422` (:2). They would queue for licenses they never use.

GameTheoryIMATMT/trial/trial.sh:1 - an `echo` statement sits above the `#!/bin/bash` shebang on line 2, so the shebang is inert. The script it runs, trial/trial.py, is one line of print("Hello World!").

Game_theory.py:14-23 - CustomStrategy.strategy falls off the end and returns None for the first two rounds, and the class is never entered into the tournament (:28 uses axl.strategies); First_game_strategies at :29 is unused.
Plot_Basic.py:33 - Slider(chosen_strategies, ...) passes a list of Player objects where an Axes is required; TypeError. Scores at :11 are np.random.randint dummies.
trial.py:67 - ax.set_size_inches(8, 6) calls a Figure method on an Axes; AttributeError every run, before plt.show(). Scores at :11 are dummies too.

Horizontal_Bar_Plot.py:83 - a verbatim StackOverflow PyQt5 scroll-plot demo over np.cumsum(np.random.randn(...)); no bar chart despite the filename, no game theory, and it builds a second QApplication at :75 after __init__ already made one at :18-21.
